heading: 8.3 Dimensioned value and bare number
text:
### 8.3 Dimensioned value and bare number [LUNI.8.3]

A number with no unit is dimensionless. It takes no dimension and no unit from
the operand beside it. A value of a `unit scalar` group ([LUNI.4.2]) is
dimensioned for this clause.

A bare number scales a dimensioned value: `x * n`, `n * x`, `x / n` and `x // n`
have `x`'s dimension. [LTIM.4.1.1] states what a `Duration` scaled this way holds.

The compiler **must** refuse a bare number beside a dimensioned value with
`DS_VALIDATE_DIM_MISMATCH` as an operand of `+`, `-` or `%`, in either order, and
in a comparison, a literal zero included. A `unit formula`'s function checks a
bare argument the same way ([LGRA.9.8.11]). `n / x` and `n // x` are [LUNI.8.4]'s.

A literal, a slot typed `Int` or `Float`, a `::Float` strip ([LUNI.8.7.2]) and a
same-dimension quotient ([LUNI.8.1]) are bare numbers. An operand whose type the compiler cannot determine is not one. This
clause does not reach the body of a unit declaration or a `unit formula` ([LUNI.4.3], [LUNI.4.5]), which is
arithmetic on plain numbers.

alloy.name: luni_8_3__bare_beside_dimensioned
alloy.note: A bare number beside a dimensioned value as an operand of `+`, `-` or `%`, in either order, or in a comparison: the clause's refusal, a transcription. A `unit formula`'s function and the literal zero are not told apart from any other bare number, as the clause has them.

alloy.name: luni_8_3__bare_only_scales
alloy.note: An accepted binop with exactly one dimensioned operand is `x * n`, `n * x`, `x / n` or `x // n`, and its result has `x`'s dimension; so no accepted `x + n`, `x % n`, `x < n` or `n / x` exists. Derived from the [LUNI.8.3] and [LUNI.8.4] refusals and the result function, within the scope; the probe holds an accepted `x * n` and `x / n`. What a scaled `Duration` holds is [LTIM.4.1.1]'s, outside the model.

alloy.name: luni_8_3__result_dim
alloy.note: A dimensioned value scaled by a bare number under `*`, `/` or `//` keeps its dimension, and under no other operator does a bare number meet a dimensioned one in an accepted binop. A transcription of the clause's scaling rule.
